data.page_description:
The National Paralympic Committee of Bangladesh (NPCB) is a para-athlete-centered non-profit national organization, affiliated with International Paralympic Committee (IPC). The committee operates under the Bangladesh Sports Council of the Ministry of Youth and Sports of the Government of the People Republic of Bangladesh. NPCB was formed in 1981 as a non-profit national organization for para-athletes. NPCB had first sent a team to the 2004 Summer Paralympics in Athens. 

NPBC is the national governing body for the Paralympic Movement in Bangladesh and responsible for promoting the Paralympic values of courage, determination, inspiration, and equality in alignment with IPC. NPBC works to develop sports opportunities for people with disabilities from beginner to elite levels.

Bangladesh's debut at the Summer Paralympics was in 2004, where it sent one athlete to compete in athletics. The NPCB was formally established in 2004 and became the official national organization for para-sports, affiliated with the International Paralympic Committee (IPC). The country has since participated in every Summer Paralympics, though it has yet to win a medal.

data.description: BROAD FF100 is a compact wall-mounted, dual-flow, single-room fresh-air system positioned by BROAD as an energy-recovery ventilator (ERV). It delivers 100 m³/h of outdoor air, filters incoming particulate matter, and exhausts stale indoor air through a separate airflow path. Its energy-recovery core transfers part of the temperature difference between incoming and outgoing air without mixing the two air streams.

data.specs_description: Laboratory-validated performance metrics and component architecture for the AIRE Products Pro S8 System.
data.features_description: A dual-flow heat-recovery architecture transfers part of the temperature difference between incoming and outgoing air.
data.feature1_desc: Designed to provide outdoor ventilation without relying on a mixed recycled-air supply stream.
data.feature2_desc: Coarse filtration protects the high-efficiency filter; the current official product information states 99% PM2.5 filtration.
data.feature3_desc: Rated power range is 5–30 W, supporting continuous ventilation with relatively low electrical demand.
data.applications_description: AIRE Products Pro S8 is engineered to exceed safety standards in the most demanding environments, from high-tech labs to daily mobility.
data.technology_description: FF100 uses a balanced, dual-flow ventilation concept. Outdoor air is drawn into the unit, passes through the coarse and high-efficiency filtration stages, and is supplied indoors. At the same time, stale indoor air is exhausted through a separate path. The two air streams pass through an energy-recovery heat-exchange core so temperature energy can be transferred while the air streams remain separated.
data.technology_card_description: Brings outdoor air toward the filtration section
data.tech_feature1_desc: Captures larger dust and protects the high-efficiency filter
data.tech_feature2_desc: Captures fine particulate matter in incoming air
data.tech_feature3_desc: Transfers sensible heat between incoming and outgoing air streams

data.question: How long do the HEPA H13 filters last?
data.answer: Under normal conditions, filters should be replaced every 120-150 hours of active use. The integrated sensor will notify you via the LED ring and app when replacement is required.

data.question: Is this product suitable for high-intensity exercise and sports?
data.answer: Yes. The active pressure balance system dynamically adjusts airflow to match your breathing rate, preventing CO2 buildup and keeping the interior cool during physical exertion.

data.question: How do I sanitize and clean the unit?
data.answer: The medical-grade silicone seal is detachable and can be cleaned with warm soapy water or alcohol-based wipes. Ensure the electronic chassis is removed before cleaning.

data.question: Does the device support Bluetooth and Smart App connectivity?
data.answer: Yes, it connects to the AIRE app via Bluetooth 5.2 and Wi-Fi for real-time air quality monitoring, filter health tracking, and firmware updates.

data.question: What is the battery life of the active sensors and motor?
data.answer: The internal lithium-ion battery provides up to 12 hours of continuous operation on a single charge. It supports fast charging via USB-C, reaching 80% in just 45 minutes.

data.question: Is FF100 an air purifier or a fresh-air ventilator?
data.answer: FF100 is a wall-mounted fresh-air ventilation system with energy recovery and filtration. It is not simply a recirculating portable air purifier.

data.question: How much fresh air does FF100 provide?
data.answer: The published rated fresh-air capacity is 100 m³/h, approximately 58.9 CFM.

data.question: Does FF100 mix recycled indoor air into the supply?
data.answer: BROAD markets the system as 100% fresh air with no mixed recycled air

data.question: How often should the filters be serviced?
data.answer: Clean the coarse filter every 1–3 months. Inspect the HEPA filter every 6–12 months and replace it sooner if airflow falls by approximately 30%.

data.question: What room size is recommended?
data.answer: The current official product information recommends approximately 10–30 m².

data.name: history_history
data.data:
{"image": "themes/default/assets/img/Air-Purify.png", "title": "History", "content": "

The history of the National Paralympic Committee of Bangladesh (NPCB) was formed in 1981. Bangladesh's debut at the Summer Paralympics was in 2004, where it sent one athlete to compete in athletics. The NPCB was formally established in 2004 and became the official national organization for para-sports, affiliated with the International Paralympic Committee (IPC). The country has since participated in every Summer Paralympics, though it has yet to win a medal.

  • 2004: Bangladesh makes its first appearance at the 2004 Athens Summer Paralympics, sending a single athlete to compete in the men's 400m T46 event.
  • 2004: The National Paralympic Committee of Bangladesh is officially established.
  • 2008: Abdul Quader Suman represents Bangladesh at the Beijing Paralympics, competing in the men's 100m T12.
  • 2012-2024: Bangladesh continues its participation in the Summer Paralympics.
  • 2022: NPCB is granted provisional membership status by the International Paralympic Committee (IPC)..
  • Present: The organization continues its work as a para-athlete-centered, non-profit national organization based in Dhaka.
"}
